events.body:

What happened and when: 22:29–22:54 pickup-to-drop-off on a RydeX fixed-fare trip charged $35.84 [F1][F2]. What is disputed: whether the driver made sexualised comments and requested the rider's number (rider's complaint) versus "small talk, nothing inappropriate" (driver statement [F4]). The only records bearing on the allegation are the rider's complaint and the driver's denial — two conflicting statements with no system record either way [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

Facts for the human reviewer to check: (i) the empty in-app chat log [F3] — it neither corroborates nor refutes a verbal exchange, since the alleged conduct was spoken, not messaged; (ii) the driver's statement [F4], which is a denial and carries no more evidentiary weight than the rider's first-hand account; (iii) whether any in-car audio, trip recording, or prior rider reports exist outside this dataset; (iv) the profile facts — rider 3.8 y, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d [F5]; driver 4.5 y, 4.86 rating, 659 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F6] — which may inform context but cannot decide the finding under the policy's treatment of profile facts [F5][F6][SAFE-1]. No route or fare issue arises: actual 17.2 km vs optimal 17.3 km (-0.1 km) and 25.9 min vs 24 min estimated are within normal variation, so the fixed $35.84 RydeX fare is not in dispute and no RD deviation or FARE add-on is engaged; no refund or fee waiver is warranted [F1][F2][RD-1][FARE-1]. Because SAFE-1 sends this to human handling, no amount is computed, no segment findings are entered, and the SAFE-1 escalation is not a conduct finding against the driver, so no account action is triggered by this ruling [F6][SAFE-1][RD-6].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint alleges harassment of a sexual nature during the trip (unwanted comments about her body and a request for her number), which is the category of conduct SAFE-1 removes from automated adjudication.

The in-app chat contains no messages between rider and driver, so the harassment is not captured in the chat log and cannot be verified or refuted by a system record; no system record contradicts the rider's account.
The driver denies wrongdoing, stating only that he 'made small talk' and that 'nothing inappropriate happened', which denies the rider's account without offering any system record in support.
The rider has a 3.8-year account with a 4.8 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days, i.e. no history of unfounded complaints, so the report is not a pattern of abusive claims.
The trip itself was normal on the system records (17.2 km actual vs 17.3 km optimal; 25.9 min vs 24 min estimated), so the fare of $35.84 is not disputed and no refund or route finding is sought.

weaknesses: There is no corroborating evidence of the harassment: F3 shows the chat log is empty, so nothing in the system records supports the rider's verbal account, and the driver's statement in F4 is a flat denial.

The rider's own account is the only source of the harassment allegation; under the rule that system records win over statements, there is no record that can confirm (or disprove) what was said in the car, which is precisely why the matter must go to human review rather than an automated outcome.
The profile history (F6) shows the driver has 659 trips in 90 days, 4.86 rating and 0 disputes/0 upheld, which the driver will use to argue the allegation is out of character.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is an allegation of verbal harassment ('comments about my body', 'asked for my number'), not an accident, injury or dangerous-driving claim, so it falls under the SAFE-1 harassment branch rather than SAFE-2 or SAFE-3.

No threat, intimidation or abusive message exists in the record: there are zero in-app chat messages between rider and driver, so there is no `chat-threat-*` item to trigger automatic escalation on the documentary record.

The driver's only recorded account is a general denial ('I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.'), and since the record is otherwise silent on the alleged comments, this is a one-word-against-the-other credibility question that no numbered clause lets me resolve automatically — it must go to human review.

The pre-ride conduct context is clean: the driver has a 4.86 rating over 659 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days, supporting that no pattern of misconduct is shown on the record.

The trip itself shows no routing or timing misconduct: actual distance 17.2 km is 0.1 km SHORTER than the 17.3 km optimal route (-0%), and duration 25.9 min is only 2.3 min above the 24 min estimate, with the fare fixed at $35.84 under the RydeX upfront model.

claims.assertion: No safety-relevant surcharge or disputed add-on is present in this case, so no refund of a waiting fee, cancellation fee or unbilled extra can arise and the $35.84 fare should stand unchanged.

weaknesses: The rider's version of the alleged comments is a direct first-hand account of the ride; the chat record is empty (F3), so there is no contemporaneous message proving or disproving what was said verbally — my client's denial (F4) is also only a statement and therefore carries no more weight than the rider's account, leaving the core allegation unresolved on the documentary record.

The 2.3 min overrun against the 24 min estimate (F2) is unexplained in the record and could be used by the other side to suggest the driver was distracted or that the ride felt uncomfortable/longer, even though it has no bearing on the harassment allegation.

My client's good standing (F6: 4.86 rating, 0 disputes) is profile evidence only, and under the policy it can support an outcome or a flag request but can never decide the finding; the rider's also-clean profile (F5) cuts the same way and neutralises the comparison.

Because the alleged conduct is verbal, there is no GPS, timeline or fare fact that can rebut it, so the system-record-wins rule gives my client no advantage here and an adverse finding remains possible despite the absence of any recorded threat (F3).

points.response: Agreed on the branch: this is an unwelcome-verbal-conduct complaint, not an accident or injury claim, so SAFE-1 is the operative clause and SAFE-2 does not apply; that branch point is not in dispute.

Conceded as a fact: F3 records no in-app chat messages at all, so there is no chat-threat-* item, and my case does not rest on a keyword match; the absence of chat merely shows the harassment was verbal and unrecoverable from records, which is why SAFE-1 sends it to human review rather than deciding it.

Accepted: F3 is empty and F4 is only the driver's denial, so on the documentary record there is one account against another and no numbered clause resolves credibility — the rider does not ask the judge to make an automated finding against the driver, only to escalate under SAFE-1.

F6 is profile evidence and, per the policy, may support an outcome but can never decide the finding; it is also neutralised by F5 (rider: 4.8 rating, 0 disputes, 0 upheld), so the driver's clean record cannot defeat the rider's equally clean report.

No disagreement: F1 shows 17.2 km actual vs 17.3 km optimal and F2 shows 25.9 min vs 24 min estimated, so the rider seeks no change to the $35.84 fare and no fee refund — the sole relief sought is human escalation under SAFE-1.

Accepted as far as it goes: an allegation of unwanted sexual comments is SAFE-1 territory and neither advocate can resolve it automatically, so my client does not seek an automated no_action finding on the harassment question.

I agree the empty chat log neither proves nor disproves the rider's verbal account, but the same absence cuts against her too: there is no `chat-threat-*` item, no threat, intimidation or abuse captured in the case file, so SAFE-1's factual trigger is unmet on the documentary record and the file is silent rather than adverse to my client.

My client's statement (F4) is exactly that — a statement — and I do not ask the judge to treat it as proof of innocence; the consequence is simply that both accounts are unverified statement evidence, and the policy gives no clause that lets either version be preferred, so no negative conduct finding can be entered against him.

The rider's clean history (F5) is conceded and I do not allege she is an abusive complainant, but profile facts are expressly barred from deciding the case, and the driver's own record (F6: 4.86 rating, 659 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is at least as consistent — so profiles net out to zero on the finding.

Agreed, and we ask the judge to record the same: 17.2 km actual vs 17.3 km optimal and 25.9 min vs 24 min estimated (F1, F2) show no route deviation and no unexplained charge, so the fixed $35.84 RydeX fare stands and no refund, fee waiver or flag is warranted.
